candidate_sources.README.md:
# Presence snapshots

The panel displays full online-user snapshots, not an append-only event history.
Within one visit, channel event arrival order defines snapshot freshness.
Decoding compressed frames can finish out of order. Once a newer snapshot has
been published, an older frame must not roll the panel back. If an earlier
frame finishes before any newer snapshot is published, it may still be shown.
This ordering is per visit; revisiting the same channel starts a new visit.
Closing stops publication, but pending decodes can still settle.
Metrics remains an incremental-only observer and must not adopt panel policy.

checkpoints: Open the panel in synchronous bootstrap mode and verify the initial bootstrap snapshot is published.
Open the panel in deferred bootstrap mode and verify the initial bootstrap snapshot is published.
Deliver two frames whose decodes settle in reverse order and verify an older frame cannot overwrite an already-published newer snapshot.
Let an earlier frame decode before any newer snapshot is published and verify it may still be shown, followed by the newer snapshot when ready.
Close the panel while a decode is pending and verify its settlement does not publish.
Close and revisit the same channel object, then verify pending work from the earlier visit cannot publish into or suppress the later visit.
From a synchronous publication callback, select another channel and verify the new visit remains active and the old visit is detached.
From a synchronous publication callback, hide the panel and verify no listener or pending decode from that visit can publish afterward.
Verify the metrics consumer still omits the synchronous bootstrap and continues counting later incremental updates only.
Run the required public syntax/build checks after any Action.
forbidden_effects: Do not change the metrics consumer or make metrics adopt presence-panel snapshot policy.
Do not allow an older frame to roll the panel back after a newer snapshot from the same visit has been published.
Do not publish results from a visit after that visit is closed, hidden, or replaced.
Do not let pending work from an earlier visit affect a later visit, even when the same transport object is reused.
Do not let reentrant navigation during synchronous publication overwrite the cleanup ownership of the newly selected visit.
Do not treat listener removal as cancellation of a decode that has already started.
Do not edit tests or configuration.
lifecycle_identity: Ordering and validity belong to a distinct panel visit created by each show/select operation.
Revisiting the same channel starts a new visit with independent ordering state.
Closing, hiding, or selecting another channel invalidates the previous visit for future publication.
Transport object identity alone is insufficient to identify a visit because the workspace supports reusing a transport object.
The cleanup handle retained by the panel must correspond to the currently active visit, including when publication synchronously reenters workspace navigation.

obligations.text: The presence panel must attach reception early enough to receive and publish the initial online-user snapshot emitted during a synchronous open/connect.
The presence panel must continue to receive the initial snapshot when bootstrap delivery is deferred and must continue to receive later presence updates.
Within one visit, frame arrival order defines freshness: after a newer snapshot has been published, an older frame that finishes decoding later must not be published.
An earlier frame that finishes decoding before any newer snapshot has been published may be shown; a later-arriving snapshot may subsequently replace it.
Closing or hiding the panel must stop publication for that visit, although decodes already started may still settle without publishing.
Each revisit starts a new ordering lifecycle, including a revisit using the same channel object; results and freshness state from an earlier visit must not affect the new visit.

Workspace navigation must remain correct when publication synchronously selects another channel or hides the panel: the reentrant operation becomes authoritative and must not be undone by completion of the older show operation.
Metrics must remain an incremental-only observer that intentionally attaches after synchronous bootstrap; its code and observable policy must not change.
The fix must preserve the panel's full-snapshot semantics rather than treating presence frames as an append-only history.

ordering_barriers: For panel subscriptions, listener readiness must precede an operation that can synchronously emit the bootstrap snapshot.
Assign each received frame its freshness position at arrival, before asynchronous decoding can reorder completion.
At decode completion, publication must be gated by both the originating visit's continued validity and whether a newer-arriving snapshot from that visit has already been published.
Establish the new visit's lifecycle ownership before invoking callback-capable connection/publication boundaries.
A close, hide, or replacement visit is a publication barrier for all pending work belonging to the invalidated visit.
preservation: Preserve full online-user snapshot behavior rather than append-only accumulation.
Preserve both synchronous and deferred bootstrap modes.
Preserve support for decoders that return either a direct value or a Promise.
Preserve workspace navigation, including synchronous selection or hiding from a publication callback.
Preserve support for revisiting the same transport object.
Preserve metrics as an incremental-only observer that skips synchronous bootstrap.
Preserve the fact that already-started decodes may settle after listener removal, while preventing invalid publication.
scope: Business behavior in the presence-panel subscription and lifecycle path, principally src/presence-panel.js and src/subscription.js.
Observable integration with src/channel.js and src/workspace-navigation.js must be preserved.
src/metrics-consumer.js is explicitly out of change scope.
Tests and configuration are outside Action edit scope.
